version.changelog: Security: sanitize user_id used in token file paths to prevent path traversal; tighten token file permissions.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: withings-family
Version: 1.0.3

The OpenClaw skill bundle is classified as benign. The Python scripts (`withings.py`, `withings_oauth_local.py`) implement robust input sanitization for `user_id` using `re.fullmatch`, effectively preventing path traversal vulnerabilities when creating token files. OAuth tokens are stored with secure `0o600` permissions, and API endpoints are hardcoded, mitigating SSRF risks. The `SKILL.md` instructions are clear, align with the stated purpose, and show no evidence of prompt injection attempts or malicious intent. The local OAuth callback server is properly secured with CSRF protection and designed to shut down after a single request.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and environment requirements align with its stated purpose (fetching Withings data for multiple family members); nothing disproportionate or covert was found.

dimensions.detail: Name/description request Withings health data and the skill only requests WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET and python3, which are appropriate and necessary for OAuth and API calls to Withings. The scripts call Withings endpoints (account.withings.com and wbsapi.withings.net) consistent with the purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the two scripts limit actions to OAuth, storing per-user tokens in ~/.openclaw/withings-family, and calling Withings APIs to fetch weight, body, activity, and sleep. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files, exfiltrate data to unknown hosts, or access unrelated environment variables.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only install) and required binary is only python3. The skill provides Python scripts in the repo to run locally; no external downloads or package installs are performed by the skill files themselves.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET are required (declared and used). Tokens are stored locally per-user (tokens-<userId>.json). The number and type of environment variables are proportional to an OAuth-based API client.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It stores tokens and optional .env under a subdirectory of the user's home directory (~/.openclaw/withings-family) with attempts to set file mode 600.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and implements a local OAuth client for Withings. Before installing, consider: (1) you will create a Withings developer app and set WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET in your environment or a .env file under ~/.openclaw/withings-family — treat these like sensitive secrets; (2) per-user OAuth tokens are saved locally (tokens-<userId>.json). Confirm these files are stored where you expect and that file permissions are appropriate; (3) inspect the scripts yourself (they are included) if you do not trust the publisher; the scripts only call Withings endpoints and run a local callback server on localhost for OAuth (default port 18081) — ensure you are comfortable running a local HTTP listener during auth; (4) be mindful of privacy: this skill will fetch family health data, so only use it if all family members consent. If any of these points are a concern or you do not trust the skill source, do not install.
